extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology record; computational and phenotypic claims are separated from direct mechanism evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Molecular docking supports a computational interaction model between all three hybrid peptides and DNA gyrase B; this is not classified as direct experimental mechanism evidence.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Docking and target fishing are computational; they suggest possible intracellular targets but do not prove direct antimicrobial mechanism in cells.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Target-fishing/docking also nominates thymidylate synthase for CATL1.2_CECB1_2 and xanthosine phosphorylase plus other receptors for CECB1_CATL1.2; these remain computational target hypotheses.
mechanism_claims.limitations: No enzyme-inhibition assay was found in local XML/PDF/DOCX materials.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: E. coli biofilm inhibition was measured phenotypically at 5x and 10x MIC, supporting antibiofilm activity context without resolving a molecular target.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: hybrid peptides tested against E. coli biofilm
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm inhibition is an activity phenotype, not a direct membrane or enzyme mechanism assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Circular dichroism evidence supports environment-dependent secondary-structure context in SDS versus buffer; this is biophysical context rather than a direct killing mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: CD spectra do not by themselves prove membrane disruption or intracellular target engagement.

source_review_notes: No local enzyme inhibition assay was found; docking claims remain computational mechanism models.
Biofilm inhibition is preserved as phenotypic activity evidence rather than molecular mechanism proof.
CD spectra are preserved as biophysical structure context and not promoted to direct membrane disruption.
